Nour Murat · Introduction

Introduction — what is FAST_PONG?

  • Capstone of the 42 common core: a single-page web app where people play Pong in 3D (Three.js / WebGL) against a friend or an AI opponent.
  • Tournaments: 3–8 nicknames, round-robin matches, automatic tie-breakers, winner announcement.
  • Player stats dashboard: games played, win-rate pie chart, best score, match history, friends list.
  • Secure access: email/password or 42 OAuth (remote authentication), optional email 2FA, JWT tokens.
  • GDPR: download my data, anonymize (42-safe), delete account, automatic inactivity cleanup.
  • Served over HTTPS by Gunicorn in Docker, PostgreSQL database, responsive on phones. Second game: Tic-Tac-Toe (local, one device) with match history; friends show an online / offline status.

Alisher Abdullaev · SDLC

SDLC model — iterative & incremental

  • We worked in short vertical slices: build a feature end-to-end → merge → fix what integration broke → next feature.
  • GitHub-flow branching: 15 pull requests merged in ~4 weeks (db-connect, game-setup, tournaments, profile-page, secure-cookies, OAuth, user-settings, delete-account …).
  • Repeated “Merge branch master into <feature>” commits = continuous integration of parallel work.
  • 86 commits, 10 Feb → 2 Apr 2025; bug-fix commits directly follow feature merges (e.g. registration fix, 2fa fixed, tournament fixed).
  • Honest note: no formal sprints, tickets or written specs are in the repo — planning happened in person; requirements came from the 42 subject & module list.

Salim Hamzaoui · Limitations

Limitations (1/2) — architecture & security

  • 42 OAuth needs a valid client key/secret in .env (the old key expired — check before the demo). The callback is now CSRF-protected by a signed, single-use state.
  • Tournaments use nicknames, not accounts (by design: users across tournaments) — tournament games are not part of personal statistics; tournament endpoints require login + CSRF.
  • Profile/settings accept the JWT or the session; the JWT lives in localStorage (XSS-readable) — mitigated by textContent rendering and HTTPS.
  • No rate limiting / lockout on login or OTP; no password reset or change.
  • Both games are local by design (PvP on one keyboard or vs AI; Tic-Tac-Toe on one device) — no online play, the remote-players module is not selected. Friends only get an online/offline status (heartbeat).
  • SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=False; debug print() of request headers in logs; avatars served via a custom endpoint because /media/ is not served when DEBUG=False.
Salim Hamzaoui · Limitations

Limitations (2/2) — operations & leftovers

  • Real OTP e-mails need a valid Gmail app password in .env; fallback: the console e-mail backend.
  • CDN dependencies (Bootstrap, jQuery, Three.js, Google Fonts) → the demo machine needs internet.
  • GDPR cron file exists but is not installed in the image → run make gdpr-cleanup manually.
  • Dead code: check_auth (wrong signing key), oauth_callback, gameapp models, django-otp installed but unused, production_settings.py.
  • Backend is one Django process (modular monolith) — fine, microservices is not a claimed module.
  • UX relies on alert() dialogs; leftover merge-conflict comments in script.js.
  • 54 automated backend tests (auth/2FA/OAuth state/presence/GDPR/tournaments/SSR) — no front-end tests.
Alisher Abdullaev · Improvements

Recommended further improvements (ranked)

  1. Keep the 42 client key and the Gmail app password valid in .env (or switch to a transactional email API).
  2. Rate limiting + account lockout on login and OTP verification; 2FA recovery codes.
  3. Store tokens in httpOnly cookies instead of localStorage.
  4. Server-authoritative Pong scores (today the client reports the result).
  5. Selectable AI difficulty; leaderboards and achievements.
  6. Vendor CDN assets locally; add password reset; CI running make test; install the GDPR cron in the image; remove dead code.
  7. Only if the remote-players module were added: online play with Django Channels / WebSockets.
Nasser Alzaabi · Fixes

What we fixed in the pre-evaluation audit (Aug 2026)

  • 2FA code “sometimes rejected” — root cause: OTP kept in per-process LocMemCache; Gunicorn runs 3 workers, so verify-otp usually hit a worker that never stored it. Fix: shared DatabaseCache (django_cache table) + reuse the code on re-login + trim/str-normalise input.
  • 2FA email “very slow” — root cause: send_mail() ran synchronously inside the login request with no timeout. Fix: background thread, EMAIL_TIMEOUT=10, failures logged — login now answers in ~80 ms.
  • make test was broken (wrong settings module) → fixed; suite grew from 2 failing tests to 54 passing.
  • Fixed the settings page saving the placeholder “The Champion” as display name when none was set.
  • Fixed the Pong ball getting stuck along the top/bottom wall: the wall bounce re-flipped every frame without pushing the ball back; it now clamps to the wall and keeps a minimum angle.
  • Fixed the previous account's avatar staying in the navbar/settings after switching users inside the SPA.
  • Second sweep on request: 30 more bugs fixed — silent JWT expiry after 60 min (automatic refresh now), secrets written to logs, duplicate-registration errors, tournament lost on refresh, repeated tiebreaker rounds, Save Settings, 2FA toggle, Pong resize/touch/pause leaks, input validation.
  • Subject-compliance pass: stored XSS via tournament nicknames fixed, AI now simulates keyboard input at player speed and anticipates bounces, DB credentials moved to .env, tournament API requires login, “Next match” announcement, GDPR anonymization (42-safe), real SSR, no 2FA toggle for 42 accounts, rule-by-rule password feedback.
  • Final pass: OAuth state parameter (signed, single-use), online/offline status of friends (heartbeat), unique display names, JWT accepted on profile/settings; an online Tic-Tac-Toe prototype was removed — no online play by design, matchmaking is the tournament system. Test suite: 54 tests.
  • Token-refresh URL bug in the SPA fixed; stale staticfiles/ now rebuilt at container start.
  • A language switcher was built on a wrong module assumption and removed again once the module list was corrected.
  • Full docs: docs/study-guide/, docs/audit-report.md.
Nasser Alzaabi · Demo

Demo cheat-sheet (1/2) — setup & accounts

Before the evaluation

  • make build && make up → https://localhost (accept the self-signed cert)
  • make test → “Ran 54 tests … OK”
  • Pre-create: demo1 / demo1@example.com (no 2FA) and demo2fa / demo2fa@example.com (2FA on) — password Str0ng!Passw0rd
  • Log in as demo1 and play 2–3 games (vs AI) so the stats dashboard has data
  • Open a 2nd browser profile to show friends between demo1 & demo2fa and the green online dot (log out → grey)

If Gmail / the 42 key are still down

  • In .env add EMAIL_BACKEND=django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend
  • make down && make up
  • Log in as demo2fa → modal appears → grep "OTP for login" gunicorn-error.log | tail -1 → enter code
  • Explain: same code path, only the transport differs
  • 42 OAuth: click “Sign in with 42” → show the authorize URL (client_id + redirect_uri); the login completes once the rotated key is in .env
